data.note:
Conclusion **Actin disruptors** confirmed. Unblinding: **latrunculin B** (PubChem CID 6436219, ChEMBL CHEMBL411879, no curated ChEMBL mechanism; BBBC021 annotates as Actin disruptors) matches protocol NSC vote 3/4 (e8).

Phenotype reflection fits literature: latrunculin B sequesters G-actin monomers inhibiting polymerization (PMID 16771841 shows inhibition of actin polymerization by latrunculin B; PMID 11514633 actin polymerization essential for polarized growth model). In MCF-7, 1 µM showed high multinucleation (frac_multinucleate_proxy z10.2, e2) = failed cytokinesis after actin contractile ring loss, while 3-30 µM showed dose-dependent tub_mean rise (rho=1.0, e9) and mitotic-like arrest (frac_mitotic_like z36.8/35.6/22.9, e3,e6,e7) with small condensed nuclei, reduced solidity and cell rounding - secondary mitotic arrest/actin loss texture captured by atlas similarity 0.75-0.81 to reference actin disruptors cytochalasin B/D, not direct microtubule stabilization despite Microscopist's visual mislead to stabilizer/Aurora mimic (e5).

Correct prioritization of NSC vote over single-stain intensity prevented misclassification.

reflection.text:
Reflection on blinded run -> unblinded latrunculin B (PubChem CID 6436219, name and BBBC021 structure agree, e14/e15) verified as Actin disruptors - correct call (protocol and scientist both Actin disruptors, 0.62).

What the evidence got right:
The high-dose quantitative image fingerprint was decisive and dose-consistent. Well w_c888e7bb46 dose 7 30 µM e3 (tub_glcm_contrast z=+171.3, tub_mean +57.9, tub_std +47.4, 259 cells), w_d76577e534 dose 5 3 µM e6 (tub_glcm_contrast +61.6, frac_mitotic_like +36.8, tub_mean +33.5, 580 cells) and w_ae9e81c96e dose 6 10 µM e7 (tub_glcm_contrast +151.6, tub_mean +50.0) all mapped by 1-NN to Actin disruptors with high similarities 0.813, 0.801, 0.752. The updated NSC vote 3/4 Actin disruptors e8 (summed similarity 2.365 vs 0.572 for the single Microtubule stabilizers vote) overrode the mixed early vote e4 (1/2 Actin, k-neighbours Eg5 6/10). This fingerprint aligns with the literature returned in this run identifying latrunculin B as inhibition of actin polymerization, e.g. PMID 16771841, and more generally with actin polymerization inhibitor phenotypes discussed in PMID 27682586. Dose response of tub_mean rho=+1.00 p=0 e9 was monotonic, consistent with a true compound effect rather than noise.

What misled or created tension:
The low-mid dose well w_19aebe57de dose 4 1 µM e2 gave extreme nuclear shape distortion (nuc_solidity -18.3, nuc_form_factor -12.3, nuc_area -10.4, 702 cells) and was 1-NN Microtubule stabilizers similarity 0.572 - the sole dissenting protocol vote. The human describe_phenotype e5 on 4 fields (density lower vs DMSO, candidates: Microtubule stabilizers, Aurora kinase inhibitors, Microtubule destabilizers) reinforced that runner-up visual interpretation. I retained Microtubule stabilizers at 0.28 in hypothesis_history step 12 for that reason, citing e5/e9/e10 as support, with e10 frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.20 p=0.8 not discriminating and e11 frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.80 p=0.2 non-significant and therefore not resolving the low-dose multinucleation vs high-dose mitotic rounding transition in my rationale. The early k-neighbour signal for Eg5 inhibitors e4 was also distracting.

Acquisition choices and what was missed:
Per list_available_experiments e1 we had 8 doses 0.01-30 µM; we acquired 1 µM + 30 µM initially then 3 µM and 10 µM (steps rationale: mid-dose moderate, high-dose maximal, then high-mid/very-high to map transition). This covered 1-30 µM well and captured the dose-consistent actin fingerprint, but left the lowest doses 0.01-0.3 µM unsampled. As the review critique noted, a lower-dose well could have sharpened the multinucleation -> mitotic arrest transition that e11 hints at, though with 4/4 wells used and no remaining budget recalibration was not mandated. We also relied on atlas vote over microscopist reading, which was correct here because the summary-feature argument for the runner-up did not account for the atlas fingerprint magnitude or the low-dose morphology.

Lesson: trust the strong, replicated high-similarity NSC signal (3/4 votes >0.75) over single-well nuclear morphology and composite-image visual calls when they conflict; explicitly flag non-significant dose-response p-values (e10 p=0.8, e11 p=0.2) as not supporting a hypothesis rather than trending evidence.
reflection.next_experiment: With unblinding confirmed: low-dose titration 0.03-1 µM with SiR-actin live labeling + phospho-H3 and cytokinesis washout vs latrunculin B reference to quantify actin-dependent multinucleation threshold, plus cell-free tubulin turbidity to exclude direct microtubule activity.
